Think of Latin esse and English "is": je suis, tu es, il est. Être is the root of the whole language.
Avoir is the twin of être. Picture a vault ("avoir" sounds like a-vault): what you have goes in it. J'ai, tu as, il a.
Sounds like "fair": a fair is where people make and do things. Fact, factory and fashion share its root.
Same root as dictate, diction and predict: things you say.
Power comes from pouvoir: if you have power, you can. Je peux = I can.
Think of voluntary and volition: what you want. Je veux = I want.
must / to have to / to owe
Linked to debt and due: you owe it, so you must do it. Je dois = I must.
Sounds like "alley": you go down the alley. The forms are irregular: je vais, tu vas, il va.
Same root as venue and convene: the place where people come together.
Think of voyeur (someone who sees) and the noun view. Je vois = I see.
Savoir-faire, "know-how", is already English. Je ne sais pas = I don't know.
A donor is someone who gives, and you donate. Same root.
Hidden in apprehend and comprehend: grabbing something. Je prends = I take.
Parliament is a building for talking, and a parley is a talk between enemies.
Think of a treasure trove: a place where you find things.
Picture a meter stick: you put it on the table to measure. Mets ton manteau = put your coat on.
Pensive means deep in thought. Je pense à toi = I'm thinking of you.
Pass, passage, passenger: almost the same word.
Credo and creed: what you believe. Je te crois = I believe you.
A porter carries bags, and portable things can be carried. In French it also means to wear clothes.
Arrive, almost identical. J'arrive! = I'm coming! / On my way!
Think of departure and parting: you leave. Je pars demain = I'm leaving tomorrow.
Sounds like "sortie", a military exit (sortie is already English). You go out.
Rest: you stay and rest. Watch out: it means to stay, not to relax.
Sounds like "tomb": you fall into a tomb. Tomber amoureux = to fall in love.
Mortal and mortuary share the root. Je meurs de faim = I'm starving.
Native, nation and nature all come from being born. Je suis né = I was born.
Vivid and vivacious: full of life. Vive la France!
Amiable and amorous come from the same Latin amare. Je t'aime = I love you.
Search comes from this very word (old French cerchier).
False friend! Demander only means to ask, not to demand. Je peux te demander? = Can I ask you?
Respond: same word. Réponds-moi = Answer me.
Comprehend, almost the same. Je ne comprends pas = I don't understand.
False friend! Attendre means to wait, not to attend. Imagine waiting forever to attend a meeting.
Looks like intend, but it means to hear. Think "I hear your intentions".
Sounds like "echo-tay": you listen to the echo.
Regard: to look at someone. Je regarde la télé = I'm watching TV.
Sense, scent and sentiment: feeling and smelling. Ça sent bon = It smells good.
Connoisseur: someone who knows a lot about something. Use it for people and places.
Appeal: you call out to someone. Je m'appelle = I call myself, my name is.
Tenacious and tenant: someone who holds on. Tiens! = Here, take this!
Laissez-faire: "let them do". Laisse-moi tranquille = Leave me alone.
Commence, same word, just more formal in English.
Finish and final. J'ai fini = I'm done.
An essay is an attempt, a try. Essaie encore = Try again.
Joy: children play with joy. Also used for playing music and sports.
Travail (hard work) gave English the word travel: long ago, travelling was hard work.
A manger is where animals eat. Mange! = Eat!
Imbibe and beverage share roots with drink words. Je bois = I drink.
Dormitory: the room where you sleep, and dormant: asleep.
Sounds like "a shut-eye": you buy a mattress to get some shut-eye. J'achète = I buy.
A vendor sells, and a vending machine sells too.
Pay, the same word. Je paie! = I'll pay!
Cost, the same root. Ça coûte combien? = How much does it cost?
Think of an oven door: you open the oven (ouvrir). Ouvre = open.
Think of firm: you close the door firmly.
Scribe and script lost their S: écrire. The accent é often hides an old S.
Legible and lecture (a reading): same family. Je lis un livre = I'm reading a book.
An apprentice is someone who learns a trade.
ay-tew-DYAY (ew: say ee with rounded lips)
Study: the S dropped and became é. étude = study.
Think of a sign: teachers show you the signs. Same root as insignia.
Demonstrate and monster (a creature shown as a warning) share this root.
A souvenir is something that helps you remember.
Re + appeler: to call again. Je te rappelle = I'll call you back.
An aide or first aid: help.
Gain: what you earn or win.
A courier runs with messages, and a current runs.
March: soldiers walk. Ça marche! = It works / Deal!
to go up / to get in
Mount: you go up a mountain or mount a horse.
to go down / to get off
Descend: going down. Je descends ici = I'm getting off here.
Turn and tour: you go around.
Voyage: a long trip. Bon voyage!
Conduct and conductor: the person who drives the train.
Ridiculous and deride: things you laugh at.
Sounds like "plural tears": lots of tears. Picture rain falling (pleuvoir = to rain).
Sous (under) + rire (laugh): a smile is a laugh held under.
Inhabit and habitat: the place where you live.
Cuisine: cooking. You already know it from restaurants.
Lavatory and lavender (used in washing): same root.
Think of neat: you clean to make it neat. Same Latin root (nitidus).
Lever and elevate: you raise yourself up.
to go to bed / to lie down
A couch: where you lie down.
Picture an ass-war: everyone fights over the chair to sit down. Asseyez-vous = Sit down.
Reveille: the bugle call that wakes up soldiers.
Habit: a nun's habit is her dress. S'habiller = to dress yourself.
An envoy is someone you send.
Receive and receipt: same family. J'ai reçu = I received.
to offer / to give (as a gift)
Offer. Je t'offre un café = Let me buy you a coffee.
Let me buy you a coffee.
Choice and choose came into English from this old French word.
Arrest: the police stop you. Arrête! = Stop it!
